info.title: Big Ball Sports API
info.description:
Unified sports data API (REST + GraphQL + WebSocket) aggregating 19+
free-tier upstream sources and 10 MCP scrapers behind a Stripe-style
gateway. Every response carries a confidence score and source attribution
so callers can render appropriate caveats.

## Pagination

List endpoints page with `?limit=` and `?offset=`. `?page=N` is an alias
for `?offset=(N-1)*limit`, resolved against that endpoint's own `limit`
default, so `?page=2` and `?offset=<limit>` are the same request. When both
are sent, `?offset=` wins; it is the more specific instruction.

Endpoints that return a single page (leaderboards, one team's form, one
player's stat line) document a `limit` and no `offset`. On those, `?page=`
is **rejected with a 400** naming `?limit=` rather than accepted and
ignored, so a paging attempt can never silently look like it worked.

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Big Ball Sports API key. Or pass via `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
Stripe-style idempotency token. Retries with the same key within
24h replay the original response without re-running the handler.

RateLimited.description:
Rate limited (`429`). Two causes share `error.code: rate_limited` and are
told apart by `error.message` and headers:
  - **Quota exhaustion** (per-minute or per-day cap). The envelope is
    enriched: `suggested_fix` names the next tier and its cap, and
    `meta.current_usage` + `meta.upgrade_path` carry live usage and the
    upgrade target. `X-RateLimit-Limit/-Remaining/-Reset` are present.
  - **4xx circuit breaker** (sustained high 4xx rate: malformed
    requests, or ignoring Retry-After and hammering past quota; key in
    cooldown). Carries `X-RateLimit-4xx-Cooldown`; no `upgrade_path`.
Additive: existing parsers keying on `error.code`, `error.message`,
`docs_url`, `support`, `meta.request_id` are unaffected.
`X-RateLimit-Limit/-Remaining/-Reset` are returned on every authenticated
response (2xx/4xx/5xx), not only on 429s, so clients can self-throttle.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the limit (or 4xx cooldown) resets.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests remaining in the tighter bucket.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix seconds at which the tighter bucket resets.

X-RateLimit-4xx-Cooldown.description: Seconds remaining on the 4xx breaker cooldown (only on breaker 429s).

message.example: Daily quota exhausted (250 of 250 requests used)

suggested_fix.example: Pace requests using the Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* response headers. Handling guide: https://bigballsdata.com/docs/rate-limits. If you're regularly at this ceiling, the solo plan is $19/month and raises your daily limit to 10,000/day: https://bigballsdata.com/dashboard/billing?plan=solo.

limiting_bucket.description:
Quota 429 only. WHICH of the two buckets refused this
request, and therefore which cap `error.message` and
`suggested_fix` are about. `current_usage` reports both
buckets without saying which one was binding; this says.

Use it for backoff: a `minute` refusal clears within
seconds, a `day` refusal not until the UTC rollover.
`Retry-After` already carries the right wait in seconds.

upgrade_path.description:
The upgrade target for THIS 429: the next tier up the
ladder, because the caller's problem is volume.
`recommended_tier` is null at the top self-serve tier.

ServiceUnavailable.description:
Service temporarily unavailable (`503`). Returned when a backing query
exceeds the endpoint's `statement_timeout` (Postgres cancels it) instead
of holding the connection for seconds. Transient under heavy load;
retry after a short delay. Standard error envelope with
`error.code = upstream_unavailable`.

archive_team_id.description: Original archive participant ID; null on match-only rows.

UnifiedNbaMatch.description: NBA's additive v1 match shape. It preserves the ordinary Match fields, adds archive identity/statistics, and preserves a date-only historical game as midnight UTC plus time_precision=date. The marker explicitly says that the time component is not a known tip-off.

NbaGameTeamBox.description: One team's box score on an NBA game row. `oreb` and `dreb` are stored team totals and always satisfy `oreb + dreb = reb` when present; they are not derived from the play-by-play log.

team_id.description: Upstream numeric team id, stable across seasons. Not a BBS team UUID.

fg_pct.description: Exact decimal ratio. PostgreSQL numeric values may serialize as JSON strings (for example, '0.455').

fg3_pct.description: Exact decimal ratio. PostgreSQL numeric values may serialize as a JSON string.

ft_pct.description: Exact decimal ratio. PostgreSQL numeric values may serialize as a JSON string.

oreb.description: Offensive rebounds. Complete for the 1985-86 season onward; null for 1984-85 and earlier, where the split was not recorded. A 0 is a real zero, not a missing value.

dreb.description: Defensive rebounds. Same coverage boundary as `oreb`.

NbaReboundSplitMeta.description: Self-teaching disclosure of what `oreb`/`dreb` are and where they stop, returned on every /v1/nba/games response.

semantics.description: What the numbers mean and how they were NOT produced.

known_gap.description: A season absent from this relation on every field, not just rebounds.

NbaPlayerSeasonAverage.description:
One player's per-game averages for one regular season, as the vendor
publishes them. Numeric fields are JSON numbers. Every column is
populated on every row we hold, so a `0` means the player really did
record none of that stat per game; it is not a placeholder for
"unknown".

season.description: Season LABEL: the year the season starts in.

min.description: Average minutes per game as "MM:SS". This is a STRING because the vendor writes it as one; we do not convert it to a decimal, because that would be a number we invented published under the vendor's name.

fg_pct.description: Field goal percentage as a ratio (0.576), not a percentage.

ft_pct.description: Free throw percentage as a ratio.

NbaPlayerAdvancedSeason.description:
One player's advanced aggregates for one season and season type.
Percentage-style fields are ratios (0.663), not percentages, except the
turnover rates and `ast_ratio`, which the vendor publishes on a 0-100
scale. `e_*` variants are the vendor's estimated counterparts to the
column of the same name.

min.description: Average minutes as a decimal. Note this differs from `min` on NbaPlayerSeasonAverage, which is an "MM:SS" string; the two relations store it differently and neither is reshaped here.

ranks.description: The vendor's league rank for each column, keyed `<column>_rank` (e.g. `pie_rank`, `off_rating_rank`). Rank 1 is best; for `def_rating` and `l_rank` that means lowest.

NflPlayerWeekStat.description:
One player's stat line for one game-week. All stat fields are returned
for every row regardless of position: a quarterback row carries 0 or
null in the defensive columns, a linebacker row carries 0 or null in
the passing columns.

Defensive columns come from the same weekly player data as the
offensive ones and cover 2020 onward at the same grain.

**TACKLE TOTALS WILL NOT MATCH `/v1/stored/matches/{id}/stats`, and that
is expected.** This dataset carries three tackle counts and no combined
total: `tackles_solo`, `tackle_assists` (assisted tackles the player
took part in) and `tackles_with_assist` (a much smaller, separate
count). The other endpoint serves a single `totalTackles` from a
different provider, at per-match rather than per-game-week grain, over
a different set of seasons.

We do NOT derive a combined total here. The usual definition is solo +
assisted, but the exact relationship between these three counts
was not verified against a reference box score, and a plausible number
computed from an unverified relationship is worse than no number; it
is indistinguishable from a correct one. Add `tackles_solo` and
`tackle_assists` yourself if you need a total, knowing that is your
definition rather than ours.

team.description: Team abbreviation the player suited up for that week.

season.description: Season LABEL: the year the season starts in.

fantasy_points_ppr.description: Standard PPR: 1/reception, 0.1/rush-rec yard, 0.04/pass yard, 6/TD, -2/int or fumble lost.

interceptions.description:
DEPRECATED and ALWAYS NULL. The loader read a column the dataset
does not carry, so this was never written in any of 112,333 rows. The
key is retained only so existing clients do not break. Read
`interceptions_thrown` or `interceptions_caught`, which say which
one they mean.

interceptions_thrown.description: Interceptions thrown by this player (the quarterback turnover stat).

interceptions_caught.description: Interceptions caught by this player (the defensive takeaway stat).

tackles_solo.description: Unassisted tackles. Not a combined total; see the schema description before comparing against totalTackles elsewhere.

tackle_assists.description: Assisted tackles this player participated in. Not interchangeable with tackles_with_assist.

tackles_with_assist.description: Tackles made WITH an assist from a team-mate. A much smaller count than tackle_assists.

tackles_for_loss.description: Tackles made behind the line of scrimmage.

tackles_for_loss_yards.description: Yards lost by the offence on those tackles.

sacks.description: Sacks credited. FRACTIONAL; a shared sack is credited as 0.5 to each defender.

sack_yards.description: Yards lost on this player's sacks. Fractional for the same half-credit reason as sacks.

fumbles_forced.description: Fumbles forced. Forcing is not recovering; recoveries are not currently served.

interception_yards.description: Return yards on this player's interceptions. MAY BE NEGATIVE; a return can be tackled behind the catch point.

defensive_tds.description: Touchdowns scored on defence. Distinct from passing_tds / rushing_tds / receiving_tds on the same row.

defensive_two_point_attempts.description: Two-point conversion returns attempted by the defence.

defensive_two_point_conversions.description: Two-point conversion returns scored by the defence.

times_sacked.description: Times this OFFENSIVE player (almost always a QB) was sacked. Distinct from `sacks` above, which is the DEFENSIVE credit.

sack_yards_lost.description: Yards lost on this player's own sacks. Distinct from `sack_yards` above, which is the DEFENSIVE figure.

passing_air_yards.description: Weekly sum of air yards on this player's pass attempts. Per-play value on GET /v1/nfl/games/{id}/plays as `air_yards`.

passing_yards_after_catch.description: Weekly sum of yards after the catch on this player's completions. Unofficial figure.

passing_epa.description: Total EPA on this player's pass attempts and sacks.

dakota.description: Adjusted EPA + CPOE composite. A published advanced metric, not derived by us.

receiving_air_yards.description: Weekly sum of air yards on targets to this player. Per-play value on GET /v1/nfl/games/{id}/plays as `air_yards`.

receiving_yards_after_catch.description: Weekly sum of yards after the catch by this receiver. Per-play value on GET /v1/nfl/games/{id}/plays as `yards_after_catch`.

fantasy_points.description: Standard (non-PPR) fantasy total. See fantasy_points_ppr for the PPR total.

air_yards_share.description: This player's share of the team's air yards this game-week. Fraction in [0,1].

pacr.description: Passing (yards) Air (yards) Conversion Ratio. A published advanced metric, not derived by us.

racr.description: Receiving (yards) Air (yards) Conversion Ratio. A published advanced metric, not derived by us.

special_teams_tds.description: Kick/punt return touchdowns. Distinct from defensive_tds and the offensive *_tds columns.

wopr.description: Weighted Opportunity Rating: 1.5 x target_share + 0.7 x air_yards_share. A published advanced metric, not derived by us.

target_share.description: This player's share of the team's receiving targets this game-week. Fraction in [0,1].

ResponseMeta.description: Response metadata. NOTHING here is guaranteed: measured over 38 live envelopes on 2026-09-18, `cached` and `request_id` appeared in 29, `source` in 28, `cache_age_ms` in 9 and `confidence` in 6. This block previously declared all five REQUIRED, which no response has ever satisfied. Treat every field as optional and branch on its absence. Routes add their own keys here (`count`, `limit`, `offset`, `note`, `total`, and per-endpoint ones), so do not assume a closed set.

date_window.description: Present when ?date= was applied. The exact window the filter used, so an omission at a day boundary is visible. start_utc is inclusive, end_utc exclusive. timezone is UTC, or the zone named by ?tz=, in which case the window is that local day. Boxing card dates are published event dates, so timezone and bounds are null there.

source.description:
Opaque source-tier label. Customers never see the vendor identity.
`forecast` marks a weather forecast (GET /v1/matches/{id}/weather).

note.description:
Short factual disclosure about something this response deliberately
withheld, present only when there is something to disclose.

On live scores it appears when `match_id` could not be resolved to a
stored match and was therefore omitted: it gives the counts and
points at `/v1/stored/matches`, whose ids you can call back into.
Absent when every served id resolves.

Distinct from `message`, which explains `coverage: false` or a stale
response. This one is attached to a response that DID serve data and
names the part of it that is deliberately missing.
note.example: match_id is omitted on 380 of 380 rows in this response. The live feed behind them does not carry an id we can resolve to a stored match, so we return no id rather than one that will not work. For rows with ids you can call back into, use /v1/stored/matches with the same sport or league, for example /v1/stored/matches?league=epl.

Envelope.description: The standard response wrapper. Only `data` is guaranteed. `error` is absent (not null) on 16 of 40 live 200 responses measured 2026-09-18, so test for the KEY before reading it; this block declared it required until then. On a non-2xx, `error` is present and `data` is absent.

value.description: The canonical value for this field. Shape varies by FieldKey.

not_outs.description: Innings ended undismissed (includes retired hurt / retired not out).

average.description: runs / dismissals. null when never dismissed.

strike_rate.description: Runs per 100 balls. null when no balls faced are recorded.

fifties.description: Scores of 50–99. A hundred counts only in `hundreds`.

overs.description: Cricket notation, e.g. "206.4" (206 overs and 4 balls). Derived from balls_bowled.

average.description: runs conceded / wickets. null when wicketless.

economy.description: Runs conceded per over. null when no balls bowled.

strike_rate.description: Balls per wicket. null when wicketless.

best_bowling.description: Best innings figures as wickets/runs, e.g. "5/23". null when wicketless.

message.example: One or more query parameters are invalid.

validation_errors.description: Structured field errors (e.g. a zod flatten) when applicable.

suggested_fix.description: A concrete corrected request, present only when unambiguously inferable.
suggested_fix.example: Lower limit to 200 or less, then walk the rest with ?offset=200, ?offset=400, … (?page=2 is an alias for the same thing).

upgrade_path.description:
Present ONLY on the two errors where upgrading is the literal
fix: the quota `429` and a plan-gate `403 forbidden`. Absent on
every other error, including the `403 key_paused` reactivation
error; a paused key is reactivated, not bought.

UpgradePath.description:
The machine-readable half of an upgrade prompt: what to buy, what it
costs, and where to buy it. Identical in shape on the quota `429` and
the plan-gate `403`, so one parser handles both, but note the two
recommend DIFFERENT things, correctly. The 429 recommends the next tier
UP (the problem is volume); the 403 recommends the LOWEST tier that
unlocks the endpoint (the problem is access), so a free key blocked on
an Edge route is pointed at Edge, never at Solo.

Every figure is real: `price` is the published list price, and
`daily_limit` and `minute_limit` are the two caps the gateway actually
enforces. Nothing here is computed from a per-request rate, and there
is no urgency or scarcity framing anywhere in these bodies.

BOTH caps are always present, because the limiter has two buckets and
either can be the one that refused you. On a `429`, read
`meta.limiting_bucket` to know which of them you actually hit.

current_tier.description: The caller's tier at the time of the error.

recommended_tier.description:
Null only where there is nothing to recommend: the top of the
self-serve ladder on a 429.

price.description:
Monthly list price. Null for a tier that is quoted rather than
listed (Enterprise), in which case `url` is the pricing page rather
than a checkout link.

daily_limit.description: Requests/day granted by `recommended_tier`; null if unmetered.

minute_limit.description:
Requests/MINUTE granted by `recommended_tier`; null if unmetered.

Added 2026-09-18. The per-minute bucket is the one a bursty client
actually hits: on 2026-09-18, the first day the gateway labelled
the two apart, 1,284 quota refusals were per-minute against 241
per-day, and until this field the object could only ever quote the
daily cap while the prose correctly quoted the per-minute one.

url.description:
Checkout, deep-linked to `recommended_tier`, whenever there is a
listed price to buy. Falls back to the pricing page when there is
not; we never deep-link a purchase that cannot complete.

StoredId.description: A stored BigBalls id. This is the identifier every match, team, player and league endpoint returns, and the one every `{id}` path segment accepts. Take it from the `id` field of the corresponding list endpoint and use it as-is.

LeagueCode.description: A short league code, not an id. `GET /v1/leagues` returns the authoritative list in its `id` field; that is the value to pass to every `?league=` parameter. Some codes accept an alias (`serie_a` and `seriea` both resolve).

CanonicalId.description: BigBalls canonical id, format `bb_<entity>_<10-32 lowercase base32 chars>`. NARROW SCOPE: the Formula 1 stored-session surface is the only place this is minted and the only place it is accepted. F1 sessions, drivers and constructors are keyed this way end to end (1,668 of 1,668 stored result rows on 2026-09-18). Everywhere else, ids are a `StoredId` and this format is REJECTED with a 400 - so do not construct one, and do not carry one across surfaces.

logo_url.description: Treat as opaque; do not construct it.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3. NOT EMITTED by /v1/teams or /v1/teams/{id} as measured on 2026-09-18; branch on its absence.

TeamAggregateStats.description: Aggregate over EVERY finished match we hold for the team, not the current season; `meta.stats_scope` restates that on each response. The goal-shaped names are used for all sports: `goals_scored` is runs in baseball and points in basketball.

TeamDetail.description: The team exactly as `GET /v1/teams` lists it, plus the `stats` aggregate that `GET /v1/teams/{id}/stats` returns. One implementation serves both, so the two cannot disagree.

headshot_url.description:
Player headshot, served from our own `/v1/assets/{id}` endpoint (or, for official league CDNs, as a direct hotlink). ALWAYS PRESENT when a route serves this field, and `null` rather than omitted when there is no image; so `'headshot_url' in player` asks whether the route serves headshots, while `player.headshot_url !== null` asks whether this player has one.

Plan-gated as a field inside a 200, never a 403: below Solo the key is present with `null` and the response carries one `meta.headshot_note` naming the plan that grants it. Solo and above get the URL. Added to `/v1/players/{id}` on 2026-09-28; it was absent there on every tier, including Pro, while `/v1/players`, `/v1/players/{id}/profile` and `/v1/stored/players` all served it.

match_id.description: Stored match id, usable as-is with `/v1/matches/{id}`, `/v1/stored/matches/{id}/stats` and the other id-taking endpoints. OMITTED when this live row cannot be resolved to a match we hold; an absent id is a condition you can branch on, an id that does not resolve is not. The scores on such a row are still real.

metric.description: Canonical metric name from a closed set.

Event.description: One play/incident row from `/v1/matches/{id}/events`. The ordering key is `sequence_number`, and there is no per-event `id` or `match_id`: the match is the one in the path. Until 2026-09-18 this schema required `id`, `match_id` and `sequence`, none of which is returned.

elapsed.description: Soccer minute from the live adapter.

clock.description: Null on feeds that carry no clock; 8 of 8 sampled baseball events were null.

home_score.description: Running home score AFTER this event.

away_score.description: Running away score AFTER this event.

coordinate_x.description: Soccer shot location: the SHOOTER's position on a 0-100 normalised pitch. `null` on non-shot events and on any event from a feed that carries no positions.

xg.description: Expected goals for a shot, 0-1. `null` means the source does not model xG for this event, never "zero chance".

xgot.description: Expected goals on target. Present only for shots that were on target; `null` for misses and blocks by design.

down.description: NFL down; null for plays without a down and for non-NFL events.

distance.description: NFL yards to gain; null for non-NFL events.

yards_to_endzone.description: NFL field position measured in yards from the opponent end zone.

yards_gained.description: NFL yards gained on the play; null for non-NFL events.

epa.description: NFL expected points added; null when unavailable or on non-NFL events.

win_probability.description: NFL possession-team win probability after the play.

defending_team_id.description: Canonical defending-team UUID on NFL rows; null otherwise.

FixtureTeamStatistics.description:
Post-match team stat line for one team. All stat fields are
nullable: a metric a league doesn't track is null, and `expected_goals`
(xG) is present only on covered leagues. Counts are integers; percentages
and xG are numbers.

StandingRow.description: One team's row in a standings table. The field names below are the ones production returns, verified identical across all 9 leagues that serve a UUID-keyed table (laliga, seriea, bundesliga, ligue1, mls, nhl, nba, nfl, mlb) on 2026-09-18. Until then this schema declared `position`, `played`, `won`, `drawn`, `lost`, `goals_for`, `goals_against`, `goal_difference` and `points`, none of which has ever been returned.

rank.description: 1-indexed position in the table AS WE SERVE IT, computed by us at read time over exactly the rows in this response, so it is always contiguous 1..N with no gaps and never null while any row in the group carries an ordering metric. `rows` are returned in this order, so the array order and this field cannot disagree. ORDERING: by the competition's own metric. For association football (sport `football`, including MLS and the Champions League) that is league points, 3 per win and 1 per draw, then goal difference (points_for minus points_against), then goals for. For every other sport it is `win_pct` as the league itself defines it. For NHL that is points percentage, (2W+OTL)/(2*GP), not W/(W+L). It falls back to wins/(wins+losses+ties) when the source supplies no win_pct. TIEBREAK, identical for every sport and applied in this order: more wins, then fewer losses, then team_name ascending, then team_id ascending. team_id makes it a total order, so the same rows always produce the same table. Teams that are genuinely level therefore get ADJACENT DISTINCT positions rather than a shared one: `rank` is a position, not a ranking class. BEFORE 2026-09-24 this field was the ingest's running counter over the vendor's conference/division tree and was NOT a table position: measured over the served rows that day, 19 of 29 adjacent NBA pairs had the lower-ranked team with the better record, and NHL (32 rows) and NCAAF (138 rows) carried null on every row. It is null now only when no row in the group carries any ordering metric at all, in which case we decline to invent one.

logo_url.description: Treat as opaque; do not construct it.

ties.description: Draws. Always present, and 0 for sports that cannot draw, so a 0 here does not distinguish "no draws" from "draws impossible"; branch on `sport` for that.

points_for.description: Goals/runs/points scored, named uniformly across sports. This is NOT competition points; no points column is served.

conference.description: The team's grouping inside the league, spelled as the league spells it. NULL wherever no grouping is recorded, which is most leagues; NULL means "not recorded", never "independent", which is itself a label ("Division I Independents"). Filter a table down to one grouping with `?conference=`.

conference_wins.description: Wins counted ONLY over matches where both teams carry the same non-null `conference`. NULL when `conference` is null.

conference_rank.description: 1-indexed position inside `conference`. NULL when `conference` is null; a rank inside no group is not a number.

Standings.description: One league's table. `/v1/standings` returns these under `data.standings`.

MatchSide.description: One side of a match. The field names are `id`/`name`; there is no `team_id`/`team_name` here. Until 2026-09-18 this schema said `team_id` + `team_name`, which no endpoint has ever returned.

logo_url.description: Served from our own asset endpoint; treat it as opaque and do not construct it.

MatchScore.description: Final or current goal/run/point totals. Null on a match with no score yet.

Linescore.description: Per-period totals. The array length and meaning follow the sport, and are not uniform even within one sport, so read it positionally only after checking `sport`.

Match.description: The match object. This one shape is returned by `/v1/matches`, `/v1/stored/matches` and `/v1/cricket/matches` alike, for every sport (verified field-for-field across all three on 2026-09-18).

league.description: The league's DISPLAY name as served here (e.g. "MLB", "NHL"). This is not the `?league=` code; see LeagueCode for that.

has_odds.description: Whether stored odds exist for this match; see /v1/matches/{id}/odds.

round.description: Competition segment as the source names it, e.g. "Regular Season - 2" or "Group Stage". This is the axis to group gameweek analytics by: a postponed fixture keeps its round while its kickoff_utc moves by weeks, so bucketing by date splits one gameweek and merges another. Free text rather than an integer, because the phase carries meaning an integer would discard. Null where the source supplies none, currently populated for soccer only.

season.description: NOT EMITTED by the list endpoints as measured on 2026-09-18. Declared because callers may hold it from older payloads; branch on its absence rather than expecting it.

venue.description: NOT EMITTED by the list endpoints as measured on 2026-09-18.

updated_at.description: NOT EMITTED by the list endpoints as measured on 2026-09-18.

dnf.description: True when the driver did not finish (mechanical

results.description: Position ranking. Empty until the results worker has processed the session.

secret.description: HMAC-SHA256 secret. Shown once at creation.

LiveScoreEvent.description:
Payload of a `score_update` / `match_start` / `match_end` frame on the WebSocket feed at wss://api.bigballsdata.com/live (Pro and above).

NOT reachable over HTTP: no path in this document returns it. It is declared here because this file is the canonical contract and the served /openapi.json is what agents and SDK generators read; a payload customers integrate against being absent from it is the same undocumented-surface problem whether or not the transport is REST.

TIMING FIELDS. `polled_at` and `emitted_at` are the two instants we can observe first-hand, and they exist so a latency-sensitive consumer can measure our segment instead of estimating it. Both are ISO-8601 with an explicit `Z` (UTC, millisecond precision), never a local offset.


  * `emitted_at - polled_at`: our internal segment, exactly.
  * `now - emitted_at`: publish, gateway relay and your own
                               transport, measured against your clock.
  * anything before `polled_at`: upstream. We do NOT decompose this
    and we do not publish an estimate of it; treat it as an upper
    bound. Our upstream is a POLL, not a push, so this segment includes
    both the upstream's own refresh cadence and our poll gap. See
    docs/live-latency-2026-09-06.md for both, measured.


No upstream-provided timestamp appears in this payload, deliberately: every time value here is a reading of our own clock.

linescore.description: Per-period scores. Null for a row with no linescore yet.

polled_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC (`Z`). The instant the upstream HTTP response was RECEIVED (response resolved, body not yet read). Reading and parsing that body, reconciling the match and writing the row all fall AFTER this instant, i.e. inside our segment. Stamped per upstream request, not per poll cycle.

emitted_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC (`Z`). The instant we published this frame to our internal bus, immediately after building it. Excludes gateway relay and socket delivery, which is why `now - emitted_at` on your side bounds them.

down.description: Current down. `american_football` only; null for every other sport, and null for a football match that is not currently live. Absence, not zero.

distance.description: Yards to go for a first down. Paired with `down`.

yard_line.description: Distance to the opponent's goal line, 0-100.

possession_team_id.description: The team currently in possession, as OUR team id, never a raw upstream id.

LivePlayerStatsEvent.description:
Payload of a `player_stats_update` frame on the WebSocket feed at wss://api.bigballsdata.com/live (Pro and above). One frame per match per poll tick, carrying only the stat cells that CHANGED on that tick.

NOT reachable over HTTP: no path in this document returns it. The closest REST equivalent is `GET /v1/live-stats/{sport}/{matchId}/players`, which returns the full current box score on demand; this frame is the same data pushed as it moves.

COVERAGE, stated rather than implied, because the four sports are NOT equivalent. Frames are published for `basketball`, `baseball`, `ice_hockey` and `american_football`. Only baseball has broad demonstrated coverage (1,290 matches carry live per-player stats as of 2026-09-07); basketball (8 matches) and ice_hockey (9) were largely out of season while the writer matured, so treat their live coverage as unproven rather than absent. `american_football` is newer still: its publisher ships BEFORE its first game, so per-player coverage begins at the 2026 season opener (2026-09-10 00:20 UTC) and nothing has been measured in play before then; subscribing today is valid and correctly silent. Subscribe to a `sport:` room to receive the `heartbeat`, which is how you tell "quiet" from "broken".

SNAPSHOT vs DELTA. `snapshot: true` means the frame carries every cell we hold for that match, sent for the first frame of a match and after a publisher restart. `snapshot: false` means it carries only what changed, so an ABSENT field means "unchanged", not "no data". Keep the last snapshot and apply deltas onto it.

STATS ARE AN ARRAY, NOT AN OBJECT. `{field, value, display}` per cell rather than `{points: 20}`. `value` is null for composite readings such as `"6-12"` (made-attempted) or a clock, which are carried in `display`; a consumer that needs a number must read `value` and handle the null rather than parsing `display`.

`player_id` and `team_id` are Big Balls UUIDs, not the ids of any upstream. `polled_at` / `emitted_at` follow the identical definition and boundaries as `LiveScoreEvent`; see that schema.

league_id.description: Null when the match has no league. The frame is still routed to its match room.

snapshot.description: True when `players` is the complete held state rather than a delta.

player_count.description: Players in this frame. Never 0: a frame is not published when nothing changed, so its arrival is itself the change signal.

stat_count.description: Stat cells across all players in this frame.

team_id.description: Null when the team is not bridged to a Big Balls id yet.

field.description: Canonical stat name. A stat we have no canonical name for yet is carried under its lowercased upstream spelling rather than dropped.

value.description: Numeric reading, or null for a composite; read `display` then.

display.description: The cell as it reads in a box score, composites included.

parameters.name: season
parameters.description:
Explicit season, labelled by the year it STARTS. Omit for the live window; an explicit past season is subject to the plan's history depth.
WHICH SEASON COUNTS AS "CURRENT" IS MEASURED, NOT A CALENDAR DATE (changed 2026-09-25). The depth a plan allows is counted back from the newest season we actually hold played matches for, not from a fixed rollover month. So while a new season is under way but has no results yet; the NHL's 2026-27 opens 2026-09-29, the NBA's 2026-10-03; the previous season stays inside the window, and the window narrows only once the new season has data to narrow to. This only ever widens what a plan reaches; it never moves the boundary earlier than the calendar rule it replaced.
`?season=` and `?date=` on this endpoint now resolve that boundary through one shared rule. Before 2026-09-25 they disagreed for the NBA and the NHL: `?season=` counted from the bare calendar year and `?date=` from the per-sport boundary, so `?sport=basketball&season=2025` returned 403 while `?sport=basketball&date=2025-12-01` returned 200 on the same key. Both are served now.

get.description:
Scoring events are included on every plan through the default view or
`?type=goals`. The full soccer minute-by-minute stream (`?type=all`,
including cards, substitutions, shots and VAR) requires Pro, matching
the NBA, NHL and NFL play-by-play floor. Where stored soccer event coverage answers
the request, `?type=goals` excludes penalties that were missed or saved
instead of mislabelling them as scored goals. Those events, and
VAR-disallowed goals, stay visible with their minute and player under
the Pro `?type=all` view. In the measured stored-event corpus, this
improves agreement with the free `score` / `linescore` fields from
22,482 of 22,755 matches (98.80%) to 22,685 of 22,755 (99.69%); 70 of
22,755 matches still require separate reconciliation.
For NBA, NHL and NFL matches, `?type=all` returns the full play log,
which is the same product as each league's dedicated plays route and
likewise requires Pro. Lower tiers receive a 403 naming the tier.
The match's sport must also be in your plan.

On `?type=all` only, NFL rows are projected from the stored NFL play
log through the match's canonical UUID. They include down, distance,
field position, yards gained, EPA and win probability when the feed
supplies them. `player_id` remains null on these rows: the upstream
player identifiers do not yet map one-to-one onto canonical player
UUIDs, so the API does not guess. The default scope and `?type=goals`
return the scoring summary without those play-level fields, which is
what keeps them available below Pro.

**Soccer shot coordinates and xG.** Where we hold shot-level data for a
match, `?type=all` also returns shot events carrying `coordinate_x` /
`coordinate_y` (the shooter's position, 0-100 normalised), `xg` and
`xgot`. Coverage is narrow and documented rather than implied: these
fields are populated for FIFA World Cup 2026 matches only, and are
`null` everywhere else. They are absent, not zero, when unknown. The
same rows are also served by
`GET /v1/stored/matches/{id}/plays`.

**`data` is ALWAYS an array, including when we hold nothing.** Until
2026-09-20 the live-router fallback arm broke that promise: a match we
do not cover returned `data: {"events": null}`, and a match served from
the live fan-out returned `data: {"events": {"value": [...]}}`, so
`data.map(...)` threw on two of the three success bodies this one path
could produce. Both now return the array, and the no-coverage signal
moved into `meta` rather than being dropped:

- `meta.coverage: false` plus a human-readable `meta.message` mean
  **we hold no events for this match**. These are the same keys
  `GET /v1/nfl/games/{gameId}/plays` uses for its empty page.
- `meta.coverage` absent with `data: []` means the match IS covered and
  the feed reports no events (for example `?type=goals` on a goalless
  match).
- `meta.count` is the length of `data`, derived from the rows sent.

An empty array and an uncovered match are different answers, so read
`meta.coverage` before concluding a match has no events.

Per-team team-stat line (possession, shots breakdown, fouls, corners,

the linescore stays authoritative for goals.
**Free plan or higher**: the box score is a raw record of the match, so
every factual field is free. One COMPUTED field is not: `expected_goals`
is omitted from both sides below the Solo plan. It is absent, never
null, so an omission is never mistaken for "no xG on record".
Stored-only: never fetches upstream. When a real match has no stats yet
(the upstream posts within ~30 min of full-time, covered leagues only) the
response is `200` with `meta.available=false` and null sides.

expected_goals_source.description: Present only when `expected_goals` for one or both sides was served from our own stored xG because the box-score feed carried the rest of the line but not xG. Measured in production 2026-09-30: 17,115 team-sides in `fixture_statistics` hold a null `expected_goals` while our stored xG covers that same match and side, concentrated in the 2015-2022 seasons of EPL, La Liga and Serie A. The live 2025/26 big-five season is NOT among them (4 of 1,756 finished matches carry a null side and none of those four is fillable), so this fills history, not today. A value the box-score feed itself carried is never replaced.

get.summary: Player stats for a season + league
get.description:
**Baseball responses carry a `level` field. Read it before summing anything.**

- `level: "match"`: `batting`/`pitching` are totals folded from real
  per-game box scores. 2026 onward.
- `level: "season"`: no per-game box scores exist for the seasons
  asked for. The numbers are full-season aggregates and are returned in
  `seasons[]`, each entry additionally marked `level: "season"`.
  `batting`/`pitching` are `null`.
- `level: "mixed"`: both are present. `batting`/`pitching` (per-game
  derived) and `seasons[]` (season aggregates) cover **disjoint**
  periods; adding them together double-counts nothing but conflates two
  different grains. Treat them separately.

A season aggregate has no home/away dimension, so `?split=home|away`
returns no `seasons[]` entries rather than full-season totals that
ignore the filter. Fields a source cannot supply (e.g. pitch counts,
which season-level history does not carry) are **omitted**, never
returned as `0`.

parameters.name: sport

parameters.description: SCOPE, not a general filter, and the same shape as ?split= below. Read ONLY on the live-upstream branch (football, cricket, mma, boxing, formula1), where it is passed through as the vendor's league id. The DB-backed branches (basketball, american_football, baseball, ice_hockey) serve one aggregate per player per sport and IGNORE it: measured 2026-09-20, ?sport=basketball with league=nba, league=epl and no league returned the same 283-byte body (hash 3ebe3df427), while ?split= over its three values returned three distinct hashes as the control.

parameters.description: Per-game splits (basketball + baseball). Season-level aggregates cannot be split and are omitted when this is set to home or away.

data.description:
Three branches were observed live on 2026-09-25, one request per sport. NO property is required, because the branches share none:

(a) `{ stats: null }`: nothing held for this player in this sport. Seen on american_football and football.

(b) per-game derived totals: `player_id, sport, season, split` plus the sport's own per-game keys (basketball: `gp, gs, ppg, rpg, apg, spg, bpg, fg_pct, fg3_pct, ft_pct`). Seen on basketball.

(c) the `level`-bearing baseball shape documented above: `player_id, sport, season, split, level, batting, pitching, seasons`. Seen on baseball.

basketball and baseball were the only sports returning numbers on the day, so the per-sport key SETS are UNMEASURED for the rest and are deliberately left open rather than guessed.

The response shape does not change; still one group per league; so a conference table and a whole-league table parse identically. A conference we do not hold returns 400 listing the ones we do, rather than an empty 200.

get.summary: What we hold, per sport and league (the discovery catalogue)
get.description:
The catalogue an agent reads to decide whether a dataset exists here, precomputed on a schedule and served from a snapshot. Every league we hold appears with its match counts, seasons, freshness and per-datatype coverage.

VOCABULARY. `data_types` is the stable default and does not change. `?v=2` adds `data_types_v2` beside it, which answers questions about a GRAIN rather than a datatype: "do you have xG" is a v1 question, "do you have PER-PLAYER xG" is a v2 one. In v2 each measure carries its grains (subject x period, e.g. `team.match` or `player.season`), every grain declares the denominator its figures count, and `not_applicable` names measures that CANNOT apply to a league as distinct from ones we simply lack. `data.vocabulary` echoes which shape was served.

v2 is opt-in because the summary answers most questions and the nested shape is only needed for grain questions. An unrecognised `?v=` serves v1 rather than failing: a catalogue call is discovery, and a query-string typo should not 400.

parameters.name: sport

get.description:
Injury reports by sport. What a row MEANS differs by league, because
injury data is a reporting artifact and leagues differ in what they
compel teams to disclose:

- `american_football`: the NFL's **mandated** weekly injury report
  `status` is a league-defined game designation:
  Out / Doubtful / Questionable. `comment` carries practice
  participation. `player.position` is always present. Published per
  week; `meta.as_of` is the date of the games that week's report covers.
  **No `return_date`**: the NFL report is designation-based and states
  no expected return, so the field is omitted rather than sent as a
  permanent null. Only rows carrying a game designation are returned;
  a player logging a full practice with no designation is not injured,
  and is not listed.
- `basketball`, `ice_hockey`: NBA / NHL reports from a paid aggregator
  (`aggregator-paid`). Note the NHL requires no disclosure at all, so
  NHL detail is vague at the league ("upper-body"), not at this API.
- `football`: soccer absences from a paid aggregator
  (`aggregator-paid`). Mostly
  **retrospective**: a record that a player missed a fixture that has
  been played, which includes non-injury absences such as suspension.
  `meta.as_of` is the newest matchday held.
- `baseball`, and everything else: not served; returns 400 naming the
  sports that are.

Endpoints that serve a stored snapshot always carry `meta.as_of` (the
currency of the DATA, never the time we last ingested it) and set
`meta.stale: true` with a plain-language `meta.message` when no fresher
data exists yet (e.g. between seasons).

get.description:
Home/away player arrays with `min_played` and a derived `played`
boolean, from post-game box scores. Self-teaching: every response's
`meta` block carries these same semantics so the payload explains
itself.

- `data_type: post_game_participation`: this is "who played", a
  strong historical availability signal for modeling. It is NOT a
  pre-tip lineup (for true pre-tip lineups, 2025-26 onward, use
  /v1/nba/games/{id}/lineups).
- Semantics: arrays contain ONLY players who logged minutes. A
  player who is absent did not play: DNP (coach decision),
  inactive, or injured, and this endpoint cannot distinguish those
  reasons. Absence never appears as `played: false`.
- Coverage: seasons 2019-20 through 2025-26 (box-score era). Games
  before 2019-10-22, preseason and All-Star games are not covered.
- For true pre-tip availability on current and upcoming games,
  cross-reference GET /v1/injuries?sport=nba (league-wide active
  injury reports) or GET /v1/players/{id}/injury. Historical
  pre-tip injury reports do not exist at our source.
- `starter` is true/false only for games with lineup coverage
  (2025-26 onward), null for earlier games; historical starter data
  does not exist at our source and we will not fabricate it.

`id` accepts a canonical match UUID or a 10-digit numeric game id
(bridged via the games list's `match_id`). A real game outside
coverage returns 200 with empty arrays and
`meta.availability_available: false`; 404 only when the id resolves
to nothing.

get.summary: NFL injuries - weekly report, practice participation and roster status
get.description: Three facts about a player, never collapsed into one. `report` is the league's mandated weekly game designation (Out, Doubtful, Questionable), `practice` is participation (Did Not Participate, Limited, Full), and `roster` is reserve-list state (IR, IR-R, PUP-R, NFI-R, Reserve-Sus, Reserve-DNR) with a human comment. A player can legitimately hold all three at once with different values, and each row's `sources` array names which feeds contributed it. 34,810 weekly-report rows cover 2020-2026, all 32 teams and every regular-season week plus the postseason rounds. Omit season to get the newest week available; meta.resolved names the season and week actually served, and meta.data_as_of is the newest updated_at in the response, which sits in the past between seasons because nothing new is published then. ROSTER STATUS IS CURRENT-INSTANT ONLY - it is attached to the newest published week and nothing else. Ask for an older season or week and every row's `roster` is null and meta.sources.roster_status.in_scope is false with a reason, rather than the field being quietly absent. Rows carrying roster status but no weekly report entry have player_id null, because player_id on this endpoint is an NFL gsis-format id and those rows have none; their identity is roster.bbs_player_id when we hold one, and otherwise their name and team. Each row's `sources` array names the feeds by WHAT THEY ANSWER - weekly_report, roster_status - never by supplier.

get.summary: NFL team-week totals - offence, defence, kicking, returns and fumbles
get.description:
Passing, rushing and receiving totals per team per week, with EPA and CPOE, plus kicking, return and fumble blocks. 3,386 rows covering 2020-2025 - 544 per 17-game season, which is every team in every game. Omit season to get the newest available; meta.resolved names what was served.
NO DERIVED `turnovers` FIELD. Sum passing.interceptions with whichever offensive fumbles-lost columns your scoring rules use. fumbles.lost_total is NOT that number - it also counts return fumbles, which the offence is not charged with.
NULL AND 0 DIFFER. kicking.fg_long is null when every attempt missed, because the stat records the longest MADE kick - absent, not zero. A null on a season that predates a load means not-loaded, never zero.
`fg_pct` is deliberately not published - it is derivable from fg_made and fg_att, and the stored value is a fraction in [0,1] despite the name.
DEFENSE. Each row carries a `defense` object: what this team's defence did in the game, derived from the OPPONENT's row in the same game, this team's summed defender credits and the final score. It is not a separate dataset, so it is available exactly where the row is. Sacks, sack yards, interceptions and yards allowed come from the opponent's offensive totals rather than summed defender credits, because a sack with no defender named is still a sack. Every defense field is null, not 0, when its input has not loaded yet (for example the opponent's row for a game still being processed).
passing_yards_allowed is NET: the opponent's passing.yards is gross, and the yards its passers lost to sacks are subtracted. total_yards_allowed is passing_yards_allowed plus rushing_yards_allowed.
THREE DEFENSIVE FIELDS ARE NOT PUBLISHED. fumble_recoveries: no stored data records who recovered a fumble. safeties: about a third of safeties (33 of 92 in 2020-2025) are team safeties from penalties enforced in the end zone, which no defender is credited with, so a credited count would silently miss them. defensive_tds: the stored defender touchdown count includes interception returns only, never fumble returns, so it is published as interception_return_tds and not as a defensive touchdown total.

get.description:
Per-player stat groups for one match, during the game and after it
finishes. One response shape for every sport listed below; cached 15s.

COVERAGE, PER SPORT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. These sports are not
at parity and this endpoint does not pretend they are.

- `baseball`: broad demonstrated coverage.
- `basketball`, `ice_hockey`: covered for the primary professional
  league only (NBA, NHL). Other leagues return a 400 naming the league.
- `football`: soccer, and only the mapped competitions (EPL, MLS,
  FIFA World Cup 2026). Anything else returns a 400 naming the league.
- `american_football`: **NFL and NCAAF (FBS) only**, from the 2026
  season opener. NCAAF FCS matches are a valid request that will keep
  returning an empty box score: the live feed does not poll that
  division, and naming it here is cheaper than letting a caller
  discover it by waiting. Before kickoff of any covered game the
  request also succeeds with `data.teams: []`, `meta.stale: true` and
  a `meta.note` saying so. It is NOT a 404: a match with no rows yet
  is a correct request whose data has not been written, and the two
  are different answers.

FRESHNESS. `meta.as_of` is the timestamp of the most recent stat cell
in the response, and `meta.stale` says whether we would expect to have
learned something more recently than that. A box score that has stopped
updating mid-game and one that is simply quiet are indistinguishable
without those two fields, which is why they are here rather than left
for the caller to infer from `fetched_at`.

player_id.description: Big Balls player UUID, resolvable against /v1/players/{id}. Null when the player is not yet linked to a player record; `name` is still populated.

starter.description: Null on `american_football`; that path does not carry it, and a guessed `false` would be worse than an honest null.

position.description: Null on `american_football`, for the same reason as `starter`. Elsewhere an object carrying the position's id, name, display name and abbreviation. Measured 2026-09-25 over the two sports that had any players on the day: 67 of 67 `american_football` rows null, 31 of 31 `baseball` rows the four-field object. `basketball`, `ice_hockey` and `football` returned 0 players, so they are UNMEASURED here, not confirmed; no `required` is declared and extra keys are permitted, because this value is passed through from the upstream boxscore.

stats.description: Positionally aligned to the group's `keys`, one entry per key, with an empty string where this player has no value for that key. Index into it by the position of the key you want; never assume a shorter array is truncated rather than shifted.

as_of.description: Timestamp of the freshest stat cell in this response, or null when the response carries none. Distinct from `fetched_at`, which is when WE answered.

stale.description: True when `as_of` is null or older than 120 seconds. A stale response is still served; this is a disclosure, not a refusal.

note.description: Present only when `teams` is empty, explaining in plain English that no per-player rows have been written for this match yet and when coverage begins.

400.description: unsupported sport, sport/match mismatch, or an uncovered league

404.description: match not found, or no live-stats coverage for it. An empty box score is NOT a 404; see the 200 above.

get.description:
Descriptive play-by-play for one match, during the game and after it
finishes. NFL, NCAAF and NCAAF FCS. **Pro plan or higher**. The shared
NFL play-by-play gate protects this route alongside the
`american_football` sport entitlement.

SOURCE, STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO AN ORDERING. `football_plays`
carries rows from two vendors; this endpoint serves ONLY the rows
from our licensed paid aggregator. The other vendor's rows exist in
storage as derivation input and are never served; that vendor's
licence is `redistribute: no`, while the paid aggregator's
all-sports redistribution grant (2026-09-09) covers this table's
rows outright.

DIFFERENT TABLE FROM `GET /v1/nfl/games/{gameId}/plays`. That endpoint
reads `public_nfl_plays` (EPA/WP, NFL only, rebuilt nightly, keyed
on the league-standard text game id). This one reads
`football_plays` (keyed on the same match UUID every other
`/v1/live-stats/*` and `/v1/matches/*` endpoint uses), sourced from
the paid aggregator and updated while a game is in progress. The two
are never blended in one response; ask for both if you want both.

FRESHNESS. `meta.as_of` is the timestamp the freshest play last
changed; `meta.stale` says whether we would expect to have learned
something more recently than that. A feed that has stopped updating
mid-game and one that is simply quiet are indistinguishable without
those two fields.

parameters.name: scoring_only
parameters.description: Return only plays where `scoring_play` is true. Accepted: true|1|yes|on and false|0|no|off; anything else is a 400 naming the parameter. false means OFF. Until 2026-09-20 every spelling of false was read as true, so opting OUT of the filter turned it ON.

kick_distance.description: Attempted field-goal distance in yards, on field-goal plays only. Null on every other play type, and null on a field goal whose text does not state a distance: an absence, never 0. Where a play describes a blocked kick returned by the defence, the returned yardage is NOT reported here: that number is the return, not the kick.

field_goal_result.description: Outcome of a field-goal attempt. `blocked` is kept distinct from `missed` because a blocked kick is not a miss the kicker owns. Null on every play that is not a field-goal attempt. `null` is listed in the enum as well as in `nullable`: an enum without it forbids exactly the value the sentence above promises, and that is the common case (176 of 179 plays on the 2026-09-25 sample).

kicker_player_id.description:
BigBalls player id of the kicker on a field-goal or extra-point attempt, the same id `/v1/players/{id}` and the post-game surfaces use, so the live feed and the box score join on an id instead of on a name.
NULL IS COMMON AND EXPECTED; DO NOT ASSUME 100% COVERAGE. Participant data is written on roughly 84% of plays (measured 2026-09-13: 81.5-85.8% per match across 11 matches), so this is null on the remaining ~16% even for plays whose text plainly describes a kick. It is also null when the play names no kicker, when the individual resolves to no player we carry, and when the id would be ambiguous; in that last case we return null deliberately rather than choose between two players. Treat null as "not stated", never as "no kicker", and do not fall back to parsing the name out of `description`: name matching is precisely the failure this field exists to remove.
Precedence when both roles appear on one play: `field_goal_kicker` wins over `xp_kicker`. Punters and kickoff specialists are NOT folded in here; they appear in `participants` under their own roles.

participants.description:
Everyone the play names, each as a role plus a BigBalls player id: passer, rusher, receiver, tackler and the rest, on the same terms as `kicker_player_id`.
Always present, but EMPTY on the ~16% of plays that carry no participant data, so `[]` means "not stated", not "nobody was involved". A member's `player_id` is null when that individual resolves to no player we carry, or would be ambiguous.
Roles observed to date: passer, rusher, receiver, tackler, sacker, fumbler, recoverer, interception_returner, penalized, field_goal_kicker, xp_kicker, kickoff_kicker, kickoff_returner, punter, punt_returner. Treat the set as open; new roles may appear without a version bump.

home_win_probability.description: NFL/paid-aggregator only, and only from the 2018 season. Null is absence, never 0.5.

note.description: Present only when `plays` is empty, explaining that no play-by-play has been written for this match yet.

400.description: invalid matchId, or sport mismatch (this feed only serves american_football)

403.description: plan does not include NFL play-by-play, or sport not entitled

404.description: match not found. An empty plays array is NOT a 404; see the 200 above.

get.summary: NHL player prop hit-rate + latest line across books
get.description:
**Requires the Edge plan or higher.** Player props are part of the
odds and model layer; Free, Solo and Trio are refused with `403
forbidden`. Moved to Edge on 2026-09-25; previously free.

For one market (shots_on_goal/goals/assists/points; saves and
power_play_points have no game-log field, so they return a real
current_line with a null hit_rate), returns the latest line we hold picked by tightest
juice plus rolling-last-N hit rate from player_stats (box
stats). 60s cache. current_line null when no nhl_player_props row
exists; hit_rate null when the player has no stats bridge or no
history.

**Check `freshness` before treating a line as a current price.** Every
response carries a `freshness` object DERIVED from the returned line's
own `fetched_at`, never from the clock: `data_as_of` (the line's real
timestamp), `age_days`, and `status` (`live` ≤2d, `recent` ≤14d,
`stale` >14d, or `no_data` when no line exists). The top-level `as_of`
is when the RESPONSE was built and says nothing about the line's age.
Between seasons the newest lines can be months old and will report
`stale`; the historical lines and the hit rate computed over them
remain valid.

**`milestones`: yes/no prop prices, separate from `current_line`.**
A milestone prop asks whether a player reaches a threshold at all, so it
is priced as ONE American `odds` integer, not an over/under pair. Each
entry is `{ sportsbook, display, line, odds, fetched_at }`, one per
(book, threshold): `goals` with `line: 0.5` is the Anytime Goal Scorer
price, `1.5` is 2+ goals, and so on.

These are strictly ADDITIVE. `current_line`, `current_line.all_books`
and the `hit_rate` line are computed from over/under rows ALONE, so a
milestone price can never appear as a line: the query keys on
`market_type` rather than leaving it to a tiebreak. The array is empty
until the milestone half of the board is being stored.

schema.description: Sportsbook short-name (e.g. betrivers). Omit for tightest-juice pick. Selects the over/under line only; `milestones` always returns every book.

over/under hit rate (model probability) beats the de-vigged over/under
juice (market probability). Edge = model minus market. Two windows:
`upcoming` (default) flags props on games in the next 24h using a
trailing `lookback`-game model; `all` runs a point-in-time historical
backtest and populates a `backtest` block (record, ROI, average edge).
The crude empirical model flags generously, so treat the backtest as a
calibration check, not an edge guarantee. Response object keys: model,
window, min_edge_pct, lookback, min_games, evaluated, value_found,
backtest (null for upcoming), props[]. 5-minute Redis cache.
**Solo plan or higher**: prop value signals start at Solo; Free
receives a 403 naming the tier and linking the docs and pricing pages.
(The `Edge` in "Edge = model minus market" above is the statistical
quantity, not the plan.)

parameters.description: Minimum model-minus-market edge in percentage points.

passing both with a conflict returns 400; omit both for all sports.
Requires a 2-way American moneyline plus an Elo rating for both teams;
a candidate whose only odds are decimal-format or a 3-way market (with a
draw) is reported in `odds_unresolved` rather than force-fit, and an
empty or partial result explains itself in `coverage_note` (null when
value games were found). Response object keys: model, window,
min_edge_pct, sport, evaluated, value_found, odds_unresolved,
neutral_site_note, coverage_note, games[], generated_at.
5-minute Redis cache.
**Edge plan or higher**: model-ready value signals start at Edge; Free
/ Solo / Trio receive a 403 naming the tier and linking the docs and
pricing pages.

`line.price` is in. The two are stored in one column with no per-row
flag, so a consumer reading `price` alone had to guess: a whole-number
decimal such as `2` or `19` is indistinguishable from an American `+2`
/ `+19` by inspection, and 900 decimal rows sit at |price| >= 100 where
magnitude cannot separate them either. The field is a FORMAT, never a

get.description:
**COVERAGE, stated plainly: this is not a per-sport prediction feed.**
Re-measured 2026-09-28 against production: 276 rows in total, and every
row is tied to one match, so the sport of a row is the sport of its
match. By sport, against that denominator of 276; football 176 (72
`match_result` for **FIFA World Cup 2026** plus 104 `value_prop`),
american_football 67, ice_hockey 29, baseball 2, basketball 2. Those
five sports are exactly what `meta.covered_sports` names. A plan scoped
to any OTHER sport receives 403 with the coverage named; a plan scoped
to one of these five is admitted and sees only its own sports' rows.
Predictions are written per batch against matches that already carry
moneyline odds, not as a continuous per-sport feed, so which of the
five sports has rows on a given day follows the odds board. (The
2026-09-02 figure of 129 rows, and its "there is no live writer" note,
are superseded: the value_prop writer resumed and added 147 rows.)

**FRESHNESS, AND WHY IT IS ON THE RESPONSE.** 129 of those 276 rows
(46.7%) are past their own `valid_until`; all 72 `match_result` rows
and 57 of the 204 `value_prop` rows, the oldest by 92 days. They are
**still returned**; nothing is filtered. Each row carries `valid_until`,
`expired` (true / false / **null** when the row states no expiry, which
is not the same as fresh) and `expired_days`, and `meta` carries
`returned`, `expired`, `expiry_unknown`, `as_of` and; only when at
least one row is expired; `stale: true` and a human `message`. An
expired row describes a match already played and must not be read as a
forecast: check `valid_until` per row before using it.

Pre-computed Elo-based win / draw / loss probabilities per match, with
value-bet analysis (Elo-implied vs de-vigged market probability) when
moneyline odds exist. Filter by `tournament` (e.g. wc2026), `match_id`,
or `type`. Requires Solo plan or higher (Free receives 403); results are
additionally scoped to the sports your key is entitled to.
Response array item keys: match_id, prediction_type, home_team,
away_team, home_win_probability, draw_probability, away_win_probability,
home_elo, away_elo, model_version, valid_until, expired, expired_days,
generated_at, kickoff_utc, plus value_bet / best_side / elo_prob /
market_prob / edge (null until moneyline odds land).

get.summary: Historical odds snapshots for a match (CLV)
get.description:
Every historical odds snapshot (opening / t24h / closing, never the live
`current` series) for one match, newest snapshot first, with sportsbook
names resolved. Powers closing-line value (CLV) and line-movement analysis.
Requires an Edge plan or higher (Free / Solo / Trio receive 403).
Each row carries an EVIDENCE-BASED `verification` field from two-source
cross-checking: a "verified" status is only ever returned when we
actually compared two providers, never inferred from the absence of a
check: `two_source_agreed` (both providers priced this book/market/side
and agreed; a positive comparison is on record), `two_source_diverged`
(both priced it and disagreed; `divergence_categories` then lists the
categories, e.g. `["PRICE_DIFF","STALE"]`), `single_source` (only one
provider carries this book/side, or the book has no cross-provider match;
NOT verified), or `unverified` (we have not compared this line; NOT
verified). The default when we lack evidence is `single_source` or
`unverified`, never a badge. `verified_at` dates the comparison the status
came from (null when nothing was compared); a verification you cannot
date is a claim you cannot check. A comparison only describes the snapshot
whose line it actually compared and only within 48h of it, so a snapshot
whose price has since moved reads `unverified` rather than inheriting an
older badge. Response: `{ data: [{ match_id, snapshot_type,
snapshot_at, market, book: { id, name, logo_url }, line, source,
fetched_at, verification, verified_at, divergence_categories? }], meta: {
total, limit, offset, snapshot_types_present, generated_at } }`.

get.summary: NHL player-prop archive: every stored observation for a game or a player
get.description:
Every stored NHL player-prop observation for one game or one player,
newest snapshot first. **16,807,052 observations across 4,231 events,
2023-05-03 to 2026-06-14**, 18 vendor markets over 9 canonical stats.
Requires an Edge plan or higher (Free / Solo / Trio receive 403).

This is the ARCHIVE. It is a different product from
`/v1/nhl/players/{player_id}/props`, which serves the CURRENT line:
one row per book and market type, picked by a stated precedence. Here
nothing is collapsed: the response grain is one observation, and season,
snapshot minute, book, market, market type, line and outcome are each
carried on their own row and each addressable as a filter. That is what
lets you reconstruct line movement yourself.

**One of `match_id` or `player_id` is required.** An unanchored window
query cannot be answered from the archive's indexes, so it is refused
rather than accepted and timed out.

**Unattributed rows are served, not dropped.** Roughly 4% of
observations name a player the bridge could not pin to exactly one of
our players. Those rows are returned with `player_id: null`, the
vendor's `player_name` intact, and `attribution` set to `ambiguous` or
`unmatched`, never guessed onto a player id. `meta.attribution_counts`
gives the split for YOUR selection. Note that a `player_id`-addressed
query cannot return them at all, by construction; `meta.
unattributed_rows_reachable` says so on every response.

**There is no `opening` or `closing` label, deliberately.** The board
opens roughly 48h before puck drop, so no stored row is provably an
opening price. Each row carries `snapshot_at` and the game's
`commence_time`, plus `before_kickoff`, which is exactly the
comparison `snapshot_at < commence_time`, made at read time. Derive
"closing" as the last observation strictly before `commence_time`.

Response: `{ data: [{ match_id, home_team, away_team, commence_time,
player_id, player_name, attribution, market, market_type, outcome, line,
price_american, book: { id, name, logo_url }, source, snapshot_at,
before_kickoff }], meta: { total, limit, offset, addressed_by,
attribution_counts, unattributed_rows_reachable, markets_selected,
snapshot_labels, generated_at } }`.

Per (match, market, canonical book) disagreements between our two odds
providers, as detected by the divergence
worker. Categories: `PRICE_DIFF` (same line, juice differs > threshold),
`LINE_DIFF` (different line value), `MISSING_FROM_ONE` (a book one
provider doesn't carry), `STALE` (one feed lagging). Requires an Edge
plan or higher (Free / Solo / Trio receive 403). Provide `match_id`, or
else `date_from` + `date_to` to bound the kickoff window. Response: `{
data: [{ match_id, sport_type, league, kickoff_utc, market, canonical_id,
book_display_name, category, secondary_categories, magnitude, detected_at
}], meta: { total, limit, offset, categories_present, generated_at } }`.
`magnitude` is category-specific (price_diff_pct for PRICE_DIFF, line_diff
for LINE_DIFF, else null) and is an ABSOLUTE difference; it carries no
direction and cannot be used to reconstruct either provider's line. The
per-provider line and price values are deliberately not returned: the
product here is the computed disagreement, not the upstream feeds.
Returns 503 while the divergence worker is still provisioning (its table
not yet created).

get.description:
Current innings state for one cricket match (overs bowled, runs, wickets, target and run rates), read from `cricket_match_state`, which the hourly cricket ingest appends to ONLY while a match is in progress.

`meta.available` is false, and `data.state` null, whenever no snapshot was ever recorded: a scheduled match, a match between innings before the first hourly capture, or any match that finished before this write path was wired (2026-08-12). That is the common answer and it is never padded with a zeroed-out innings.

`meta.live` describes the PAYLOAD, not the match: true only when the match is in progress AND a snapshot exists. For a finished match the last recorded snapshot is returned with `live: false` and a note, so a closing reading is never mistaken for a current one. `recorded_at` carries the observation time in every case.

`required_run_rate` is present only where it can be computed honestly (T20-format chases); it is omitted for ODIs and Tests rather than derived from an assumed innings length.

parameters.description:
Return the newest snapshot for THIS innings instead of the newest snapshot for the match. `cricket_match_state` is append-only and per-innings, so a multi-innings match holds state for each innings it was captured during; without this parameter only the last one is reachable. get.description:
Conditions at a match's kickoff. For a kickoff in the past these are OBSERVED values, for one in the future they are a forecast; `forecast.observed` says which, so a caller never has to infer it by comparing the kickoff against the clock. The shape is identical either way.

`forecast` is null, with a machine-readable `unavailable_reason` and a prose `note`, whenever conditions cannot honestly be attributed to the kickoff. Branch on `unavailable_reason`, never on `note`.

For an entitled caller, a valid match id returns 200. `404 not_found` means only that no match exists with that id. Missing venue data or coordinates are coverage gaps represented by a 200 response, not a claim that the caller supplied the wrong id.

Outdoor weather at an enclosed stadium describes the car park, not the game, so it is withheld rather than served. `venue.roof` is returned so a consumer can render "Indoor" instead of a blank.

A `retractable` roof is withheld on the same grounds: the roof's STATE at a given kickoff is a property of the match, we have no source for it, and a guess is indistinguishable from a fact in the response.

venue.description: The resolved venue, or null when none is known. Coordinates are null when the venue is known but has not been geocoded.

roof.description: Whether the venue is open to the sky.

apparent_temperature_c.description: Feels-like temperature: wind chill in the cold, heat index in the heat.

observed.description: true = measured after the fact, false = predicted beforehand.

unavailable_reason.description: Stable reason that forecast is null.
